examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify independent subproblems, a shrinking parameter and combine cost. Prove a combine invariant using correctness of smaller subproblems. Logarithmic depth does not imply logarithmic total work: all subproblems at every level count. Memoization changes work when subproblems overlap.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A recurrence creates four size-n/2 children per node and stops at size 1. For n=8, how many leaves occur?

**Answer: 64.** There are log₂8=3 splitting levels. Four-way branching gives 4³=64 leaves, equal to n². The depth is only three but the leaf count is quadratic.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Overlapping recursion can repeat work exponentially. A recurrence for the return value may differ from the recurrence for runtime.

Splitting into halves does not automatically imply logarithmic total time; all recursive branches contribute.
